questions.answer: As \(x\to0^+\), the values of \(x\) are positive and get closer to zero. Dividing \(1\) by a very small positive number gives a very large positive number. Therefore \(\lim_{x\to0^+}\frac{1}{x}=\infty\).
As \(x\to0^-\), the values of \(x\) are negative and close to zero. Dividing \(1\) by a very small negative number gives a very large negative number. Therefore \(\lim_{x\to0^-}\frac{1}{x}=-\infty\).

questions.prompt: Find the one-sided limits of \(f(x)=\frac{1}{x-2}\) as \(x\to2\).
questions.answer: As \(x\to2^+\), the denominator \(x-2\) is small and positive, so \(\frac{1}{x-2}\to\infty\). As \(x\to2^-\), the denominator is small and negative, so \(\frac{1}{x-2}\to-\infty\). Thus the right-hand limit is \(\infty\) and the left-hand limit is \(-\infty\).

For \(x\ne3\), the square \((x-3)^2\) is always positive. As \(x\) approaches \(3\), this positive denominator approaches \(0\). A positive number divided by a very small positive number grows without bound. Therefore \(\lim_{x\to3}\frac{1}{(x-3)^2}=\infty\).

As \(x\to1^+\), the numerator \(x+2\to3\), which is positive. The denominator \(x-1\) is small and positive. A positive number divided by a small positive number tends to \(\infty\). Therefore the limit is \(\infty\).

As \(x\to1^-\), the numerator \(x+2\to3\), which is positive. The denominator \(x-1\) is small and negative. A positive number divided by a small negative number tends to \(-\infty\). Therefore the limit is \(-\infty\).

questions.prompt: Determine whether \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1}{x}\) exists as a two-sided infinite limit.
questions.answer: Check both sides. As \(x\to0^+\), \(1/x\to\infty\). As \(x\to0^-\), \(1/x\to-\infty\). Because the one-sided limits have different signs, there is no single two-sided infinite limit. Therefore \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1}{x}\) does not exist as a two-sided limit.

questions.prompt: Find the one-sided limits of \(f(x)=\frac{x}{x^2-4}\) as \(x\to2\).
questions.answer: Factor the denominator: \(x^2-4=(x-2)(x+2)\). Near \(x=2\), the factor \(x+2\) is positive and close to \(4\), and the numerator \(x\) is positive and close to \(2\). The sign is therefore controlled by \(x-2\). As \(x\to2^+\), \(x-2>0\), so the limit is \(\infty\). As \(x\to2^-\), \(x-2<0\), so the limit is \(-\infty\).

Factor \(x^2-4=(x-2)(x+2)\). As \(x\to-2^+\), the numerator \(x\) is negative. The factor \(x-2\) is negative, while \(x+2\) is small and positive. The denominator is therefore negative times positive, so it is small and negative. A negative numerator divided by a small negative denominator tends to \(\infty\).

questions.prompt: For \(f(x)=\frac{2x-1}{(x+1)^2}\), find the infinite limit as \(x\to-1\).
questions.answer: As \(x\to-1\), the numerator approaches \(2(-1)-1=-3\), which is negative and non-zero. The denominator \((x+1)^2\) approaches \(0\) through positive values from both sides. A negative non-zero numerator divided by a very small positive denominator tends to \(-\infty\). Therefore \(\lim_{x\to-1}\frac{2x-1}{(x+1)^2}=-\infty\).
